lxc_6b02a5837ce3b870.text: For about 400 years, a medieval crane stood on top of Cologne Cathedral's unfinished south tower.

lxc_bfe0f761ac0c1da5.text: During those same centuries, a perfume created by an Italian in 1709 made the city's name famous across Europe.

lxc_c8457ee9646eb610.text: Imagine standing in Cologne after building work on the cathedral had stopped.

lxc_0bcbab1b2fcd6b34.text: You look up at the cathedral, but it isn't finished.

lxc_8148025de5efd4fb.text: A huge wooden crane sits on one tower.

lxc_e41d1ea27f9a4a5a.text: This half-built church raises a simple question: why would anyone start such an enormous building and then leave it?

lxc_dd1b224e00833ed7.text: To answer that, we first need to know why it was started.

lxc_a904a0f60f3d86a8.text: In the 6th century, after Roman rule ended, Merovingian kings built a church for a bishop there.

lxc_42cace7c2576623c.text: Centuries later, Cologne's archbishops wanted something much bigger.

lxc_9190f6bd2123152d.text: They built the Gothic cathedral and new city walls together.

lxc_b2c23a4e84cd3e5e.text: Their aim was to promote Cologne as a "Holy" city and as the capital of their Electorate, the region they ruled.

lxc_24617d2568ad3749.text: So the cathedral was about faith, but it was also about power and image.

lxc_73da29a83409a8e6.text: By 1322, the eastern end, called the choir, was finished and consecrated.

lxc_27ada6da2ea4efed.text: That means it was officially made holy and could be used for worship.

lxc_2e8e1ca1db260a32.text: Much of the early money came from pilgrims.

lxc_72c173d90fd51532.text: These were travellers who came to visit the Shrine of the Three Kings inside the cathedral.

lxc_92a49790cbe73918.text: Think of the cathedral like a business that depends on visitors.

lxc_3d2dd58da76b7dd8.text: When many visitors arrive, the work can continue.

lxc_31bd8715f09fd50d.text: The key point for the rest of the story is that the building relied on money from outside the city.

lxc_e2752adbaaf9b110.text: Many people assume the cathedral took so long because medieval builders were slow.

lxc_f79c4ba8d56e9f6c.text: The choir was finished in about 74 years.

lxc_3e46d3e581fefd4c.text: The long delay came later, and it had clear causes.

lxc_2be04b9f79716be9.text: Income from pilgrims declined, and by 1473 the funding had stopped.

lxc_1fd60cdad269a56f.text: In 1473, work stopped with the south tower built up to the level of the bells.

lxc_b3c2d84f9fa0e700.text: A large crane was left standing on it, and it stayed there for 400 years.

lxc_195643f547013457.text: In 1474, Cologne needed its craftsmen for something more urgent.

lxc_311dde4ec06cb690.text: The city had to strengthen its defences against the Duke of Burgundy.

lxc_8e289f35bde43730.text: When your city is under threat, walls matter more than towers.

lxc_a180691e615d1e7f.text: The third problem was religious change.

lxc_a5e2fa80f856ab99.text: The cathedral had also earned money from indulgences.

lxc_703283ec7ede2bfb.text: These were payments connected to the forgiveness of sins.

lxc_b13f054b777dceec.text: The Reformation challenged this practice, and that income was lost.

lxc_3eb9928f8909de2f.text: By around 1560, construction had stopped completely.

lxc_f564144ee6537cbf.text: Notice how each cause made the others worse.

lxc_0e08f45e9ff18ebb.text: Fewer pilgrims meant less money, and war took away the workers.

lxc_6669cef2b3fded34.text: After that, the Reformation removed another source of income.

lxc_ff0aa10d85840d72.text: The story did not end there.

lxc_352c7ffa19716204.text: Efforts to restart began around 1814, and work started again in 1823.

lxc_1d3012a45d58a60f.text: However, proper funding only arrived in the 1840s.

lxc_596b62a699e27a68.text: The builders completed the long main hall, the side arms and the towers in the 19th century.

lxc_268cf71d5bfba1ab.text: They used the medieval plans to do it.

lxc_b2071ff9eb91a59d.text: The cathedral was still unfinished, and the old crane was still on the tower.

lxc_7d2f54a87c5ce1b0.text: In that year, an Italian named Johann Maria Farina created a new fragrance in Cologne.

lxc_2665a702f86ea474.text: He made it from citrus oils and alcohol.

lxc_118b95a3808de73a.text: He was inspired by the memory of an Italian spring morning after rain.

lxc_b44a7504b4892037.text: One of Cologne's most famous products came from an outsider.

lxc_85a1b2ee5f374d97.text: Its feeling came from Italy, but its name came from Cologne.

lxc_85f04bf43a551dab.text: Every bottle that travelled abroad carried the city's name with it.

lxc_b01626c364dc1987.text: Famous customers made this effect much stronger.

lxc_258450288cce66f9.text: Napoleon, the writer Goethe, Queen Victoria and Empress Elisabeth all used Farina's Eau de Cologne.

lxc_dc44172192f483a1.text: Napoleon is said to have used two bottles a day.

lxc_fd94ddb53142c57d.text: When powerful and admired people use a product, others want it too.

lxc_ea20c5ac797d4103.text: In this way, the perfume made Cologne world-famous.

lxc_892b9421fdde5942.text: At first, a cathedral and a perfume seem to have nothing in common.

lxc_82c719c895960659.text: One is made of stone and the other is a scent.

lxc_e55d41271f2e1f0d.text: But both stories follow a similar pattern.

lxc_76cf4920e7ee3ad0.text: First, both depended on people from outside.

lxc_97fcc81f727d8d58.text: Pilgrims' money built the cathedral, and the work stopped when that money stopped.

lxc_f7d7f28998498e12.text: An Italian created the perfume, and famous foreigners spread its name.

lxc_3c1709a1ff940783.text: In both cases, Cologne's fame was built partly by others.

lxc_82289fce6c40b61d.text: Second, both stories are about keeping old work alive.

lxc_6798c05a95873519.text: The cathedral was finished with medieval plans, centuries after the first stone was laid.

lxc_01e200566bc0d602.text: The Farina company was founded in 1709 and is the world's oldest fragrance maker.

lxc_7ab390a18125cfc3.text: Farina family descendants still make the original Eau de Cologne in the city today.

lxc_6d28a82e38f78dda.text: Since 1723, the company's headquarters has been the Farina House, which is now the Fragrance Museum.

lxc_51e8f9257480f595.text: So let's return to the old idea that medieval builders were simply slow.

lxc_5adb9a21cb09eae9.text: They finished the choir in a lifetime.

lxc_cd5539e146d3479a.text: The cathedral waited because pilgrim income declined, craftsmen were needed for the city's defences, and the Reformation cut off money from indulgences.

lxc_45057bcd3a4da48e.text: Cologne's story is less about slowness and more about dependence and patience.

lxc_f5019e6790e60868.text: The city relied on pilgrims and customers, and it kept returning to unfinished work.
